title: Module 15 · Mixed Patients (Top 10%)
intro: Real patients cross modules. Each case stacks problems the way a night shift does: magnesium plus infection plus kidneys, sepsis plus renal dosing, a bleed caused by a dosing error, crush injury, DKA with QT risk, postpartum clots while breastfeeding, HIT history and falling platelets.

cases.title: Magnesium, fever and falling urine
cases.stem: On magnesium 2 g/h for 10 hours. Now temperature 39 °C, fetal tachycardia: intraamniotic infection. Urine output 20 mL/h for 3 hours, SCr up from 0.6 to 1.3. Weight 90 kg. No allergies.

steps.q: Before any antibiotic, what do you do about the magnesium?

options.t: Check reflexes, breathing and a serum magnesium level now; ask the team to lower the rate (label: 1 g/h maintenance in severe renal impairment or oliguria, max 20 g per 48 h)
options.why: Low urine output means magnesium is building up.

options.t: Nothing, magnesium does not depend on the kidneys
options.why: Magnesium is cleared by the kidneys.

options.t: Ampicillin 2 g IV every 6 hours plus gentamicin
Vancomycin alone

steps.q: How do falling kidney function and magnesium change your gentamicin thinking?

options.t: Kidney function is changing, so avoid assuming normal clearance: use levels and dose by kinetics; and know magnesium plus aminoglycosides both cause neuromuscular blockade
options.why: Gentamicin label warns about neuromuscular blockade with other blocking drugs. Watch breathing closely.

options.t: Give 7 mg/kg by the Hartford nomogram
options.why: Pregnancy and unstable kidney function are Hartford exclusions.

cases.call: **S/B:** On magnesium 2 g/h, new intraamniotic infection, urine 20 mL/h, SCr 0.6 to 1.3. **A:** Magnesium is accumulating, and gentamicin adds kidney and neuromuscular risk. **R:** Magnesium level and reflex check now, lower magnesium to 1 g/h per label, start ampicillin 2 g q6h plus gentamicin with levels guided dosing, and I will follow her kidney function.
cases.pearl: **One patient, three risks: magnesium build up, aminoglycoside kidney injury, and stacked neuromuscular blockade.**

sources.t: Magnesium Sulfate in 5% Dextrose label (MedLibrary)
ACOG Committee Opinion 712: intrapartum management of intraamniotic infection. Obstet Gynecol 2017
Gentamicin injection prescribing information (DailyMed)
St. Mary's protocols for each step (verify locally)

workup.calc: Urine 20 mL/h x 3 h (60 mL in 3 h, goal 75 mL) and SCr doubled: lower to 1 g/h per label, level now. Gentamicin adds kidney and neuromuscular risk.

cases.title: Septic shock with failing kidneys
cases.stem: Septic shock from a pneumonia, 80 kg, CrCl 25 mL/min. Norepinephrine 0.3 mcg/kg/min for 5 hours. Orders: vancomycin 1,000 mg, cefepime 2 g every 8 hours, pantoprazole.

options.t: Load 20 to 35 mg/kg actual weight (for example 2,000 mg), not reduced for kidneys; then choose maintenance by kidneys and levels
1,000 mg because of the kidneys
Give the full first dose now, then adjust maintenance for CrCl 25 to avoid neurotoxicity
options.why: FDA alert: neurotoxicity mostly with kidney impairment and no adjustment.

options.t: 2 g every 8 hours continued
Hydrocortisone 200 mg/day (pressor 0.25 or more for over 4 hours)
Add vasopressin rather than raising norepinephrine
Stress ulcer prophylaxis is indicated (shock)
Tight glucose 80 to 110

cases.pearl: **Septic shock + bad kidneys: full loads, adjust maintenance, steroids, vasopressin, SUP.**

sources.t: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021. Crit Care Med 2021;49:e1063-e1143
Rybak MJ, et al. Vancomycin consensus guideline. Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864
FDA safety alert: cefepime and nonconvulsive status epilepticus (2012)
SCCM/ASHP 2024 stress ulcer prophylaxis guideline

cases.title: The fall, the bleed, and what comes next
cases.setting: ED to neuro ICU · elderly woman
cases.stem: 84 years old, 58 kg, fell at home. ICH on CT. Apixaban 5 mg BID for AF (SCr 1.6). SBP 188.

options.t: 4F-PCC per protocol, SBP target about 140 (not below 130)
Vitamin K and SBP below 110
Andexanet
options.why: Withdrawn from the US market in 2025.

steps.q: Looking back at her home dose, what do you notice?

options.t: She meets 3 of 3 apixaban reduction criteria (age 80+, weight 60 kg or less, SCr 1.5+), so her dose should have been 2.5 mg BID
options.why: An overdose contributed to bleeding risk. Report it and fix it before any restart.

options.t: Her dose was correct
Heparin or enoxaparin prophylaxis is reasonable 24 to 48 hours after the bleed is stable
Never

cases.pearl: **Reverse, control BP, then find the error that set it up (wrong apixaban dose).**

Kcentra prescribing information, DailyMed

workup.calc: Age 84, weight 58 kg, SCr 1.6: **3 of 3** reduction criteria: her home dose should have been 2.5 mg BID.

cases.title: Crush injury, day 3
cases.stem: Crush injury 3 days ago. CK 48,000, K 6.8 with peaked T waves, urine output falling. On gentamicin for an open fracture. Now needs reintubation.

options.t: Calcium first, then insulin and dextrose (consider 5 units with kidney injury), then remove potassium (binder, dialysis)
Calcium lowers potassium, so that is enough
Rocuronium; avoid succinylcholine (crush injury after 24 to 48 hours and K 6.8)
options.why: Succinylcholine can cause a hyperkalemic arrest.

options.t: Succinylcholine
Rhabdomyolysis and falling urine output: ask whether a non nephrotoxic option covers the fracture, and check levels if it continues
Continue without change

cases.pearl: **Crush day 3: no succinylcholine, treat K in 3 steps, and rethink nephrotoxins.**

sources.t: KDIGO dyskalemia conference. Kidney Int 2020;97:42-61

cases.title: DKA with pneumonia
cases.stem: DKA, K 3.1, Mg 1.4, QTc 510. Chest X ray: lobar pneumonia, not severe. Orders: insulin drip, ceftriaxone, azithromycin, ondansetron.

options.t: No: replace potassium to 3.5 or more before insulin (2024 consensus); replace magnesium too
Yes

steps.q: What is the hidden danger in this order set?

options.t: QTc 510 with low K and low Mg, plus azithromycin and ondansetron (both prolong QT): torsades risk
options.why: Fix electrolytes and consider a non QT prolonging plan.

options.t: None

steps.q: Which CAP option avoids adding QT risk?

options.t: Ceftriaxone plus doxycycline (the ATS/IDSA alternative when a macrolide should be avoided)
Levofloxacin alone

cases.pearl: **Low K, low Mg, long QT: fix electrolytes, then choose drugs that do not stack QT.**

cases.title: Postpartum clot while breastfeeding
cases.stem: Day 4 after cesarean, new PE. Breastfeeding. BP 158/98 on two readings. Pain orders include acetaminophen with codeine.

steps.q: Which anticoagulants are compatible with breastfeeding?

options.t: Enoxaparin
options.why: Large molecule, minimal milk transfer, not orally absorbed by the infant.

options.t: Warfarin
Apixaban
options.why: Labels advise against breastfeeding on DOACs (limited data).

options.t: Labetalol, nifedipine ER or enalapril
options.why: The pregnancy ban on ACE inhibitors ends at delivery.

options.t: Lisinopril is contraindicated because she was pregnant
options.why: Not after delivery; enalapril is the studied option.

options.t: Avoid codeine (and tramadol) while breastfeeding; use scheduled acetaminophen and ibuprofen, short low dose oxycodone if needed
Fine

cases.pearl: **Breastfeeding: enoxaparin or warfarin, labetalol or nifedipine or enalapril, no codeine.**

sources.t: LactMed (NIH): warfarin, enoxaparin, enalapril, codeine
Eliquis prescribing information (lactation section), Pfizer
ACC: antihypertensive medications in pregnancy and lactation (2026)
FDA: codeine and tramadol in breastfeeding (2017)

cases.title: Warfarin bleed in a patient with HIT history
cases.stem: GI bleed, INR 6.8 on warfarin. Allergy list: "heparin: HIT 2023."

options.t: No: Kcentra contains heparin and is contraindicated with known HIT
Yes
Vitamin K 10 mg IV plus plasma (FFP), with the team weighing volume, or a heparin free factor product if St. Mary's stocks one
Nothing; wait for vitamin K

steps.q: Which other heparin exposures do you block for this patient?

options.t: Heparin flushes and heparin coated catheters
Enoxaparin
Nothing else

cases.pearl: **HIT history: no Kcentra, no heparin flushes, no enoxaparin.**

sources.t: Kcentra prescribing information, DailyMed
ASH 2018 HIT guideline. Blood Adv 2018;2:3360-3392

cases.title: Falling platelets on day 15
cases.stem: Day 15 of linezolid. On sertraline and heparin 5,000 units SC q8h since admission. Platelets 210,000 to 95,000. No new clot.

options.t: Linezolid myelosuppression (usually after about 2 weeks)
HIT is possible, but the timing (day 15) and another clear cause lower the 4Ts score
Lab error only

steps.q: What else about linezolid and sertraline?

options.t: Serotonin syndrome risk: monitor and discuss
No interaction
Calculate the 4Ts with the team, consider HIT testing if intermediate, and ask ID about an alternative to linezolid
Transfuse platelets

cases.pearl: **Low platelets: list every cause (drug, HIT, sepsis). Linezolid after 2 weeks is a classic.**

ASH 2018 HIT guideline. Blood Adv 2018;2:3360-3392
